title: 1984 AHSME Problem 10
statement: Four complex numbers lie at the vertices of a square in the complex plane. Three of the numbers are \(1+2i,\) \(-2+i\) and \(-1-2i.\) The fourth number is

solutions.text:
The points \(1+2i\) and \(-1-2i\) are opposite vertices, so their midpoint \(0\) is the center of the square. The fourth vertex is therefore the reflection of \(-2+i\) through the origin, namely \(2-i.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Two of the listed vertices are opposites
Their midpoint is the square’s center, so reflect the remaining given vertex through that point
